name: POS (Part-of-Speech) Sequence Variation
description: Analyzes the diversity and predictability of syntactic structures by tracking the sequence and distribution of Parts-of-Speech (POS) tags. AI generators tend to rely on structurally formulaic sentence patterns (e.g., standard Subject-Verb-Object constructions with predictable adjective placements), leading to less variance in how grammatical tags are sequenced across the text compared to the chaotic, rhythmic variations of human writing.
algorithm: Syntactic N-Gram and POS Distribution Profiling
mechanism: The algorithm first parses the text using a dependency parser or POS tagger to convert all words into their grammatical categories (Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives, Prepositions, etc.). It then calculates two primary metrics: 1) POS Distribution (the overall frequency ratio of each tag, where AI often overuses determiners and generic adjectives) and 2) POS Sequence Variation (the entropy of 3-gram and 4-gram POS sequences). Human writers frequently break grammatical conventions for stylistic effect, use complex dependent clauses, and interject irregularly, creating a high entropy of POS sequences. AI-generated text, optimized for fluent but safe generation, heavily favors the most statistically probable grammatical structures, resulting in repetitive, highly predictable syntactic rhythms (e.g., 'Determiner + Adjective + Noun + Verb' repeated endlessly). The system compares these observed sequences against human baseline corpora to compute an artificiality score.
useCase: Highly effective for analyzing formal essays, news articles, and professional writing where structural mimicry by AI is common.
strengths:
• Highly robust against simple vocabulary substitution attacks (like changing 'utilize' to 'use') because the underlying grammatical skeleton remains unchanged.
• Operates at a structural level, making it highly cross-compatible with different topics and domains.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives in highly structured, formulaic human writing (such as legal documents, technical manuals, or standardized test essays).
• Requires a sufficiently long text (usually >150 words) to accurately map the structural distribution and sequence entropy.
parameters:
Analysis: POS Tagging (Universal Dependencies) and Syntactic N-Gram Entropy
Metric: POS Transition Probabilities and Tag Distribution Ratios
Output: 0-100 Syntactic Predictability (Artificiality) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-85% accuracy. Very strong when combined with lexical and perplexity-based methods, as it analyzes the 'skeleton' rather than the 'flesh' of the text.

references.title: Fröhling, L. & Zubiaga, A. (2021). Feature-based Detection of Automated Language Models: Tackling GPT-2, GPT-3, and Grover. PeerJ Computer Science.
